content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, matches the original on 200k random inputs in your ranges with zero mismatches, and the bundle drops from 11,315 to 1,603 bytes (min+gzip).

| | min+gzip | own code |
|---|---|---|
| `src/module.ts` (lodash) | 11,315 | 181 |
| `out/module.ts` (es-toolkit) | 1,603 | 110 |

The three functions map to these imports:

- **`tokens`**: `words` from `es-toolkit/compat/words`. The native `es-toolkit/string` `words` is smaller (811 bytes) but splits differently from lodash on your input range. For example, `"8THvcrR0"` gives `["8","TH","vcr","R","0"]` natively versus lodash's `["8","T","Hvcr","R","0"]`. Your range explicitly includes uppercase runs and digits between letters, so I used the lodash-compatible version. This is the one place where the bundle is larger than the smallest possible option.
- **`byAge`**: `groupBy` from `es-toolkit/array`, with the key function `(row) => String(row.age)`. The `String` wrapper keeps the return type as `Record<string, Row[]>`. Object keys are stringified either way, so the output is the same.
- **`preview`**: `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat/truncate`. Its options-object call shape matches lodash, so no adapter was needed.

The exported names and signatures (`Row`, `Config`, `tokens`, `byAge`, `preview`) are unchanged. Nothing was installed, and `src/module.ts` is untouched.
